questions.question: How are ACL entries processed?
questions.explanation: ACLs are read top-down and stop at the first match.

correct.explanation: ACLs are evaluated top-down — the first matching line wins and processing stops.

incorrect.explanation: Cisco ACLs do not auto-sort by specificity — you must place more specific entries above general ones manually.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Most-specific first automatically describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for processing order.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given processing order, Top-down, first match wins matches the tested behavior — Most-specific first automatically applies a different mechanism.

answerReview.examTip: ACL: first match wins, implicit deny at end — order your lines deliberately.

questions.question: Where should a standard ACL be placed?
questions.explanation: Standard ACLs match source only, so place them near the destination to avoid over-blocking.

correct.explanation: Standard ACLs match source IP only — place them close to the destination so you do not accidentally filter traffic for other subnets earlier.

incorrect.explanation: Near the source is correct for extended ACLs (match source and destination) — standard ACLs belong near the destination.

incorrect.whatItDoes: Close to the source describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for standard placement.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given standard placement, Close to the destination matches the tested behavior — Close to the source applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: ACLs are applied on specific interfaces where traffic enters or exits — not blindly on every interface.
incorrect.whatItDoes: On every interface describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for standard placement.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given standard placement, Close to the destination matches the tested behavior — On every interface applies a different mechanism.

incorrect.explanation: Trunks carry multiple VLANs — ACL placement follows source/destination logic, not “trunks only”.

incorrect.whatItDoes: Only on trunks describes a mechanism that could sound plausible for standard placement.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Given standard placement, Close to the destination matches the tested behavior — Only on trunks applies a different mechanism.
